newsitem.title: UK: Sun Life upbeat on UK life insurance market.
newsitem.headline: Sun Life upbeat on UK life insurance market.

text.p: UK insurer Sun Life & Provincial Holdings Plc said on Thursday it was pleased with its first set of results since flotation and was well placed to maximise profits from the recovery in the British life assurance market.
The group, which brings together Sun Life, UAP Provincial and New Ireland Holdings, reported pro forma pre-tax profits of 92.5 million pounds ($144 million) for the six months to June 30, 1996.
"We are very pleased with the results," the group's chief executive, Michael Hart, told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Hart said the British life market seemed to be recovering, although the sector remained highly competitive.

Sun Life, which was floated on the London Stock Exchange in July and in which France's UAP retains a majority stake, provides life assurance, pensions and investment products to both individuals and businesses in Britain.
Hart said the unit had not had to sacrifice profit margin in order to maintain its market position.
He said UAP Provincial, the general insurance unit, would stand up well in terms of underwriting profit with its competitors. "We think it will stand comparison in the market place," he added.
Motor insurance rates were starting to go up and Hart said he envisaged rises of between two and four percent. "There will be room for some more (increases) later in the year," he said.
Hart said other insurance rates were still very soft. He believed there would be a turnaround, but not before mid or late 1997. The change would take place because margins would be squeezed too much.
But UAP Provincial was not as exposed to rate-cutting as other insurers because it had mainly small ticket business. ($1=.6415 Pound)
